planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil; part of the ruffled-leaf Dressed Up series, the largest-growing of the trio.

directions: Dressed Up Evening Gown Coral Bells builds a substantial mound of glossy, near-black leaves with deeply ruffled margins that catch light differently than typical matte heuchera foliage. Tall, airy flower scapes rise well above the leaves in summer, carrying pink buds that open to white blooms attractive to pollinators. Site it in evenly moist, well-draining soil with some afternoon shade to keep the dark foliage from scorching, and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor. Its larger habit makes it a strong anchor plant for shaded borders rather than a typical container filler.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil; the compact member of the ruffled-leaf Dressed Up series.

directions: Dressed Up Prom Dress Coral Bells forms a tidy, compact mound of heavily ruffled pewter-toned leaves etched with dark charcoal veining, with new growth emerging in a contrasting violet flush. Short flower stalks appear in summer above the foliage mound, though the plant is grown primarily for its long season of textured leaf color. Keep soil consistently moist but well-drained and provide some shade from hot afternoon sun to preserve the cool foliage tones through autumn. Its small, dense habit suits container plantings and the front edge of shaded beds.
